incident-bot: INCIDENT 1970012345 — KV_CACHE paging spike detected on quantized runtime (int8/awq path). Auto-escalation triggered :rotating_light:
Maya Chen: I'm oncall. Getting a pager for sustained paging from GPUs. Latency up ~3x for affected models, request errors increasing. Looking at node metrics now.
Raj Patel: Seeing huge KV cache footprint growth on awq-int8 kernels. Evictions skyrocketing, swap I/O on host increasing.
Theo Morgan: Stack traces point to kernel selection switching to awq fallback for specific attention patterns — kernel behaviour increases per-token KV size.
Lina Ortega: Customer-facing: multiple enterprise customers reporting timeouts for chat route. Emma, any customer impact numbers?
Emma (CS): We have 4 customers with >10% request errors and ~2 customers with live sessions dropped. Raising to SEs for outreach.
Maya Chen: Initial mitigation plan: 1) throttle continuous batching for affected model routes 2) force kernel fallback to fp16-path for the hot routes 3) increase eviction aggressiveness temporarily. Will coordinate rollouts.
Carlos R: Quick config snippets to roll a hotfix:
```
# reduce continuous batching to favor latency
redwood config set continuous_batching.max_batch_tokens=512 --route chat/v1
redwood config set continuous_batching.max_concurrent_batches=2 --route chat/v1
# force kernel selection to safe path
export REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=fp16_fallback
# increase eviction
redwood config set kv_cache.eviction_target_ratio=0.6
```
Raj Patel: Deploying config changes to canary pool A now. I'll keep batch window small and monitor eviction rate.
Theo Morgan: Also enabling temporary prefix-KV caching disable for the problematic prompts (reduces overall KV growth). Command: `redwood route update --name chat/v1 --disable-prefix-kv true`
Maya Chen: Rolling canary to 10% traffic at t+6m. Watch: per-node swap, kv-cache-evictions/sec, request latency P95.
incident-bot: Canary rollout started: 10% -> routes: chat/v1 -> pool: canary-A.
Raj Patel: Early signal: eviction rate down ~45% on canary, P95 latency down ~25% vs impacted baseline. No new OOMs.
Emma (CS): Notifying affected customers that we're mitigating and will follow up with root cause; prepping incident comms.
Lina Ortega: Question: can we do an automated fallback to fp16 when KV footprint > X? We should avoid manual toggles in the future.
Theo Morgan: We have a flag but it's not enabled for awq kernels. Filing a follow-up to add a dynamic kernel-fallback policy tied to kv_cache.size_ratio.
Carlos R: For immediate relief I'm pushing a manual kernel fallback to the rest of affected nodes (force kernel env). Executing now.
Maya Chen: Full rollout to all pools at t+22m. Metrics: errors dropping, P95 close to baseline but throughput reduced ~8% due to smaller batches. Acceptable tradeoff.
SupportBot: Automated note: incident severity set to SEV2; oncall handoff scheduled in 3h.
Emma (CS): Customers updated; one customer asked for timeline on a permanent fix — told them engineer follow-up within 24h.
Raj Patel: Root-cause hypothesis: quantization kernel (awq-int8) computes denser KV representations for specific head/seq combos causing memory blowup. Kernel selection heuristics failed to detect pathological sequences.
Theo Morgan: Action items: (1) add KV-size guardrails in kernel selector (2) add metric to track per-request kv footprint (3) test auto-fallback thresholds in staging with long-context prompts.
Maya Chen: Handoff to night oncall (Theo) in 2h. I'll update the incident doc with mitigation steps and metrics. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident update posted to #incidents and #sre-oncall.
